list.name: Restarts
list.textFormat: process_start_time_seconds changed (crash, OOM kill or kill-service)

list.name: Flag flips
list.textFormat: runtime flag switched from the control plane

description: Postgres pools and queries (app side), Postgres server (postgres-exporter), Redis (app side and redis-exporter), caches, Redis streams, the dead-letter queue and the transactional outbox.

panels.title: Waiting for a connection
panels.description: Requests queued for a pooled Postgres connection. If waiting > 0 while idle == 0 the pool is exhausted — see lab pool-exhaustion. Usual cause: something holds connections too long (slow query, row lock wait, pg_sleep chaos), not a pool that is too small.

panels.title: Idle connections
panels.description: Connections open but not checked out. 0 idle + waiting > 0 = exhausted. Many idle connections in every service also cost Postgres memory (max_connections is 400 for the whole cluster).

panels.title: Busy / open / max connections
panels.description: busy = checked out, open = busy + idle, max = configured pool size (dbPoolSize, dashed). Once busy reaches max, new requests queue (see Waiting for a connection).

targets.expr: max by (service) (db_pool_connections{service=~"$service", state="total"}) - max by (service) (db_pool_connections{service=~"$service", state="idle"})

panels.title: Pool utilization
panels.description: Checked-out connections / pool size: the U in USE. 100% alone is not a problem; 100% with requests waiting is saturation (lab pool-exhaustion). Dashed: 100%.

targets.expr:
(max by (service) (db_pool_connections{service=~"$service", state="total"}) - max by (service) (db_pool_connections{service=~"$service", state="idle"}))
/
max by (service) (db_pool_connections{service=~"$service", state="max"})

panels.title: Connection acquire time p99
panels.description: How long a request waited to get a connection. Any value close to dbAcquireTimeoutMs (3s) means callers are about to fail with acquire_timeout.

panels.title: Acquire timeouts
panels.description: Requests that gave up waiting for a connection (db_errors_total{code="acquire_timeout"}). These become 503 UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE for the customer.

panels.title: DB errors by code
panels.description: Errors by Postgres SQLSTATE: 40P01 deadlock_detected (lab deadlocks), 57014 statement timeout (lab slow-search), 53300 too_many_connections, acquire_timeout (pool exhausted), connection (Postgres unreachable).

panels.title: Query latency p99 by op
panels.description: p99 per logical query (op), including the wait for a connection. One slow op (an ILIKE '%q%' scan) holding connections slows every other op on the same pool. Lab: slow-search.

panels.title: Queries per second by op
panels.description: Query throughput per op. A listing endpoint that issues 1 + N queries shows a query rate far above its request rate. Lab: n-plus-one.

panels.title: Queries per HTTP request
panels.description: SQL queries issued per inbound HTTP request (1m). Batched code stays at 1-3; N+1 code scales with page size (24 products -> 25 queries). Dashed: 10 (QueryAmplification).

panels.title: Failed queries by op
panels.description: Queries that ended with outcome=error. Deadlock victims, statement timeouts and acquire timeouts all land here.

panels.title: Deadlocks
panels.description: Deadlocks detected by Postgres per minute (pg_stat_database_deadlocks). deadlock_timeout is 200ms, so each one also cost ~200ms of lock waiting before Postgres picked a victim. Lab: deadlocks.

panels.title: Backends by state
panels.description: Postgres backends by state (pg_stat_activity). 'idle in transaction' holds locks and a connection while doing nothing — a classic pool-exhaustion cause. Dashed: max_connections.

panels.title: Locks by mode
panels.description: Locks held or awaited, by mode (postgres-exporter lower-cases them). With inventory.reserve=select_for_update, buyers of the same hot SKU queue on each other's row locks; each waiter shows up as an extra sharelock on the holder's transaction id (lab oversell-race). Long waits also appear in 'Longest open transaction'.

panels.title: Transactions per second
panels.description: Commits and rollbacks per second. Rollbacks rise with deadlocks, timeouts and aborted checkouts.

panels.title: Longest open transaction
panels.description: Age of the oldest transaction per backend state. A long 'active' transaction is a slow query; a long 'idle in transaction' is application code holding a transaction open while it does something else.

panels.title: Replica lag
panels.description: How far the order-history read replica is behind the primary (db_replica_lag_seconds, from orders). Reads inside this window miss recent writes. Lab: replica-lag.

panels.title: Replica lag over time
panels.description: Lag itself is normal. The bug is sending a customer's read right after their own write to the replica (orders.readConsistency=replica) instead of the primary (read_your_writes). Compare with the loadgen anomaly order_missing_after_pay. Dashed: 1s (ReplicaLagHigh).

panels.title: Clock offset by service
panels.description: Each service's business clock minus real time (clock_offset_seconds). Negative = behind (the sale has not started yet for it); positive = ahead (passes and reservations look expired early). Beyond ±1s time-based logic breaks (ClockSkew). Lab: clock-skew.

panels.title: Redis p99 by op (app side)
panels.description: Latency of Redis operations as the services measured them. Redis itself answers in microseconds; anything in the milliseconds is network, client queueing or injected latency (chaos redis). Lab: redis-blip.

panels.title: Redis p99 by service
panels.description: Same latency per calling service.

panels.title: Redis errors
panels.description: Failed Redis operations per service. Sessions, carts, rate limits and the waiting room all depend on Redis: compare how each feature degrades (rate limiter fail_open vs fail_closed).

panels.title: Redis server commands/s
panels.description: Commands processed by the Redis server (redis-exporter) and the busiest command types.

panels.title: Redis memory
panels.description: Memory used by Redis (carts, sessions, caches, streams). maxmemory is 768 MiB with noeviction: at the limit writes fail.

panels.title: Redis clients
panels.description: Connected and blocked clients. Blocked clients wait on blocking commands (XREADGROUP BLOCK).

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Lookups served without a rebuild (hit, l1_hit, stale) / lookups that consulted the cache (bypass excluded). A cliff right after a TTL expiry or flush-cache is the start of a stampede. Lab: cache-stampede.

targets.expr:
(
  sum by (cache) (rate(cache_requests_total{service=~"$service", result=~"hit|l1_hit|stale"}[30s]))
  or
  0 * sum by (cache) (rate(cache_requests_total{service=~"$service", result!="bypass"}[30s]))
)
/
sum by (cache) (rate(cache_requests_total{service=~"$service", result!="bypass"}[30s]))

panels.title: Cache lookups by result
panels.description: hit (Redis), l1_hit (in-process), stale (served old value while one request refreshes), coalesced (waited for an in-flight rebuild — single-flight), miss (rebuilt from Postgres), bypass (caching disabled).

panels.title: Cache rebuilds per second
panels.description: Entries reloaded from Postgres. With naive TTLs a hot key expiring triggers one rebuild per concurrent request; with single-flight it is one rebuild per key.

panels.title: Concurrent rebuilds (stampede meter)
panels.description: Rebuilds in progress right now, summed across processes. Dozens of concurrent rebuilds of the same cache is a stampede: every one of them is a Postgres query holding a pool connection. Dashed: 20 (CacheStampede).

panels.title: Consumer lag
panels.description: Entries in the order stream not yet delivered to the consumer group. Growing lag + flat processing = head-of-line blocking (lab poison-pill).

panels.title: Pending (unacknowledged)
panels.description: Entries delivered but not acknowledged (Redis PEL). A message retried forever stays pending forever.

panels.title: Messages processed by result
panels.description: ok, failed (will be retried), dead_lettered (moved to the DLQ after 3 attempts).

panels.title: DLQ length
panels.description: Messages parked in the dead-letter queue. Non-zero is fine operationally (the consumer moved on) but somebody must inspect and replay or discard them.

panels.title: Outbox backlog
panels.description: Order events written to the outbox table but not yet relayed to the stream. Safe (they are in Postgres) but delayed.

panels.title: Event publishing
panels.description: Order events by publishing mode and result. dual_write failures are events lost forever (committed order, no event); outbox relays retry until they succeed. Lab: lost-events.
